title: Channelopathy anchor -- measured biology validates the threshold DIRECTION

anchors.measured_phenotype: congenital insensitivity/indifference to pain (no pain under any circumstance)
anchors.citation: Cox et al. 2006, Nature 444:894; Goldberg et al. 2007, Clin Genet 71:311

anchors.threshold_direction: firing threshold lowered (gate opens too easily)
anchors.citation: Drenth et al. 2005, J Invest Dermatol 124:1333; Yang/Waxman lineage
Fertleman et al. 2006; Estacion et al. 2008, J Neurosci 28:11079

anchors.measured_phenotype: congenital insensitivity to pain with anhidrosis (CIPA)

anchors.threshold_direction: firing threshold RAISED (gate held closed) -- the realised analgesic move
anchors.measured_phenotype: approved non-opioid analgesia for moderate-severe acute pain
anchors.citation: suzetrigine (VX-548/Journavx), FDA approval 2025-01-30; Vertex Phase-III program

intervention_summary.pathological_pole: threshold LOWERED / barrier REDUCED (GOF channelopathy or up-regulation)
intervention_summary.protective_pole: threshold HIGH (innocuous input stays sub-threshold; CIP at the limit)
intervention_summary.analgesic_direction: controlled RETURN toward the protective pole (raise |h_sp| / restore barrier)
intervention_summary.selectivity_principle: intervene at nociceptor-restricted effectors (Na_V1.8 > Na_V1.9 > Na_V1.7 by peripheral selectivity) so motor/CNS function and reward circuits are spared -> the non-addictive, non-sedating corollary, a-priori from the read and now FDA-validated by the Na_V1.8 case

honesty: DIRECTION/ORDER anchored to measured phenotypes; NO quantitative clinical magnitude asserted.
